title: Installing the plugin
description: This installs an external package that this project has not installed, so nothing here is compiled or run by this site.

title: Enabling it in Next.js
description: The reactCompiler option became stable in Next.js 16. It also needs the separate package babel-plugin-react-compiler, which is not installed in this project. Next.js only applies the compiler to relevant files, which limits the build cost.

title: Testing an interaction with React Testing Library
description: This uses separate packages that are not installed in this project, along with a DOM environment such as jsdom. It reads like what a person does: find the button, click it, and see the result.

title: A first test
description: This needs the external packages @testing-library/react and jsdom, which are not installed in this project. getByRole throws if there is no match, so finding the element is itself an assertion.

title: Typing and submitting
description: This requires the separate package @testing-library/user-event, which is not installed here. Finding the field by its label also verifies that it is labelled.

title: The usual query
description: screen comes from the separate package @testing-library/react, which is not installed here. This finds a button by role and accessible name.

title: Adding an item
description: This depends on the separate packages @testing-library/react and @testing-library/user-event, which are not installed here. It also assumes a TodoApp in your own code.

title: Closing a dialog with Escape
description: This uses external packages that are not installed in this project. jsdom does not do layout, so visual focus and scrolling still need a real browser.

title: One interaction
description: user and screen come from a separate package, not installed here. This finds the button as a user would, then clicks it.

title: Waiting for loaded data
description: This depends on the separate package @testing-library/react, which is not installed here, and on a UserName in your own code. It checks the loading state, the result, and that loading has gone.

title: Waiting for a non-DOM outcome
description: This uses external packages that are not installed in this project. Since a mock being called does not change the DOM, findBy would not work here, so waitFor is the right tool.

title: Waiting for an element
description: screen comes from a separate package, not installed here. This waits for the alert, and it finishes as soon as it appears.

title: A Hook behind a test component
description: This uses external packages that are not installed in this project, and it assumes a useToggle in your own code. The test does not depend on how useToggle stores its value.

title: Testing a Hook’s interface
description: This depends on the separate package @testing-library/react, which is not installed here, and it assumes a useCounter in your code. initialProps only applies to the first render, and act is needed since nothing else wraps this update.

title: Rendering a Hook
description: renderHook comes from a separate package, not installed here. result.current then holds the Hook’s latest return value.
